newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China Travel to raise HK$2.5 bln.
newsitem.headline: China Travel to raise HK$2.5 bln.

text.p: China Travel International Investment Hong Kong Ltd said on Tuesday that it planned to raise HK$2.5 billion after expenses through a share placement and issue of new shares.

The company said in a statement that its majority shareholder, China Travel Service (Holdings) Hong Kong Ltd, would sell 420 million existing shares to institutional investors at HK$3.60 each and subscribe to 700 million new shares at the same price.

The net proceeds are intended to be used for investment projects and purchase of assets, including toll roads, hotels and investments in passenger transportation and freight forwarding businesses, China Travel International said.
The placement and subscription shares represent 18.5 percent and 30.8 percent, respectively, of the company's existing share capital, it added.
The placement price represents a 4.6 percent discount to Monday's closing price of HK$3.77. Trading in China Travel International shares was suspended on Monday afternoon.
Following the transactions, China Travel Service's holding in the company would be diluted to 60.2 percent from 66.5 percent, it said.
The new issue is conditional upon the approval of independent shareholders and regulatory approval, it added.
The placement was arranged by Goodwill Investment Services, CEF Capital and Jardine Fleming Securities, China Travel International said.
